findings.problem: The contact approach/recovery target evaluation passes timeMs clamped between contactMs and recoverMs to goal(), which freezes the goal time to recoverMs instead of holding the contact goal time during the held phase and spatially clamping moving carry/pick-place goals. In addition, when gestures use custom carryOffset, goal() evaluates the Cartesian path while sampleNativeContactArm() blends shoulderDeg directly towards the activeTarget solved at that goal. When timeMs is during the approach or recovery phase, evaluating goal() at contactMs rather than evaluating the exact static contact point forces the angular interpolation target to jump prematurely, breaking the C2 angular approach towards the true contact grip.
findings.fix: Pass the goal evaluated at gesture.contactMs (or gesture's exact held contact point) as the fixed contact reference activeTarget to sampleNativeContactArm, ensuring contact goal time is bounded to its held phase for angular approach/recovery rather than spatially clamping or prematurely advancing moving goals during approach/recovery.

findings.problem: sampleNativeContactArm asserts that error (hypot between end and activeTarget) is <= 0.001 whenever weight === 1. However, during a moving pick-place or carry transition between contactMs and recoverMs, activeTarget is being evaluated at a single contactMs/held time or static grip while the hand moves, causing the exact grip check to throw Error('needs-view-manipulation: owned hand lost its exact grip') when activeTarget differs by more than 0.001px from the real-time goal.
findings.evidence: Lines 65-66: const error=weight===1?Math.hypot(end.x-activeTarget.x,end.y-activeTarget.y):0; if(error>.001)throw new Error('needs-view-manipulation: owned hand lost its exact grip');
findings.fix: When weight === 1 during ownership, evaluate the chain against the current-time active contact target (weight=1 during ownership without spatial clamping), ensuring exact owned grip under the original body clock matches the true instantaneous contact target.

findings.problem: nativeContactWindow incorrectly defaults recoverMs to g.endMs for action==='carry' without checking whether g.releaseMs is provided or whether carry is exiting, and for action==='drop' it can compute recoverMs that exceeds landingMs or fails to align with g.releaseMs when omitted, causing mismatch with the compiler goal() timeline which relies on CARRY_TRANSITION_MS and explicit releaseMs.
findings.evidence: Line 34: const recoverMs=g.releaseMs??(g.action==='carry'?g.endMs:g.endMs-Math.min(220,(g.endMs-g.startMs)*.18)); Lines 572-581 in compiler.ts use explicit release and CARRY_TRANSITION_MS.
findings.fix: Require and validate explicit releaseMs for drop/carry actions that complete within the clip or align default recoverMs strictly to the action's release/drop transition timing.

limitations: Review is strictly bounded to provided source files and review excerpts; no tools or execution runtime available.
Artwork, anatomical realism, palette, voice, and production gates remain unverified and unapproved.
